identity.title: TD-JEPA: Latent-predictive Representations for Zero-Shot Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Learn representations that support unsupervised, zero-shot reinforcement learning across tasks and policies.

gap.claim: Existing approaches are typically restricted to single-task learning, one-step prediction, or on-policy trajectories, leaving long-term multi-policy prediction from offline, reward-free transitions insufficiently addressed.

contributions.claim: Introduces TD-JEPA, combining TD-based latent-predictive representations with unsupervised RL.
Trains explicit state and task encoders, a policy-conditioned multi-step latent predictor, and parameterized policies to enable test-time zero-shot optimization of arbitrary reward functions.
Reports theoretical results on non-collapse, low-rank long-term policy dynamics, and latent successor features, alongside benchmark results across 13 datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish TD-JEPA by using TD learning to obtain long-term, multi-policy latent predictions from offline, reward-free transitions for unsupervised RL.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that an idealized TD-JEPA variant avoids collapse with proper initialization and learns encoders capturing a low-rank factorization of long-term policy dynamics, while its predictor recovers latent successor features.

The authors report that TD-JEPA matches or outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on locomotion, navigation, and manipulation across 13 ExoRL and OGBench datasets, especially for zero-shot pixel-based RL.

narrative_sequence.summary: Latent prediction is presented as a paradigm for learning general representations, with RL applications spanning auxiliary losses, reward-based and unsupervised RL, behavior cloning, and world modeling.
The paper identifies common scope limits in existing methods and argues that TD learning enables long-term latent-dynamics prediction across policies using offline, reward-free transitions.
TD-JEPA applies this idea to unsupervised RL through state/task encoders, a policy-conditioned multi-step predictor, and latent-space parameterized policies.
The resulting system is described as supporting test-time zero-shot reward optimization, with theoretical analysis and benchmark comparisons across 13 datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a precise limitation of prior methods with a mechanism—TD learning—that addresses long-term, multi-policy prediction from offline reward-free data.

lessons.interpretation: A strong abstract can make its motivation legible by linking a narrowly stated gap directly to the proposed technical principle.
lessons.application: Frame a new method by naming the exact data, horizon, or task restriction it targets, then state which design choice is intended to relax that restriction.
lessons.exception: Avoid this framing when the work is primarily exploratory and no single mechanism is clearly tied to a defined limitation.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative scores, baseline identities, dataset-level breakdowns, or experimental protocols.
The theoretical claims are qualified to an idealized variant and proper initialization; the abstract does not specify how these conditions relate to the evaluated system.
